[1] A significant portion of this BEV drop, nearly two-thirds, was attributed to a decline in Tesla Model 3 registrations, while plug-in hybrid electric vehicles (PHEV) continued to show strong growth. This information was reported by news outlets such as Reuters on the same day. <3> In a report published on May 13, 2024, the consultancy Metals Focus projected that the average price for rhodium is expected to fall by 28% to $4,750 per troy ounce for the 2024 calendar year. [17] In response, mining companies began implementing cost-cutting measures, curbing capital expenditure, and considering workforce reductions to remain viable. [6, 12, 15] <5> A report from the Rhodium Group revealed that US investment in clean energy and transportation surged to a record $67 billion in the fourth quarter of 2023, marking a 40% increase from the same period in 2022. The report, published on February 29, 2024, also highlighted that the fastest investment growth occurred in emerging climate technologies, which saw a tenfold annual increase from $0.9 billion in 2022 to $9.1 billion in 2023. The project will be implemented in two phases, with the initial phase involving confirmatory piloting and a feasibility study at Lifezone's labs in Perth, Australia. This first phase, expected to be completed in the first half of 2024, is funded with $3 million, contributed equally by both companies. Upon successful completion, the second phase will involve the joint funding and construction of a commercial-scale recycling facility in the United States, with an estimated initial capital cost of $15-20 million. <7> On February 24, 2023, the White House announced new import tariffs on a range of Russian products, which were officially published in the Federal Register on March 2, 2023. Effective April 1, 2023, the United States government imposed 'dissuasive' import taxes on certain Russian goods, including a 35% ad valorem tariff on Platinum Group Metals (PGMs) such as platinum, palladium, and rhodium. While overall imports from Russia have significantly decreased since 2022, the U.S. continues to import strategic commodities, including PGMs like palladium. These tariffs and other sanctions are intended to disrupt Russian revenue. However, analysts note that the global PGM market is resilient, and Russian metals often continue to flow by being rerouted to other sanction-agnostic regions. Russia remains a major global supplier of PGMs, accounting for a significant portion of the world's primary supply. <8> In January 2023, the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) offered a conditional loan commitment of up to $700 million to Ioneer Ltd for its Rhyolite Ridge lithium-boron project in Esmeralda County, Nevada. The primary purpose of the project is to develop a domestic supply of lithium carbonate for electric vehicle batteries, with boron as a valuable co-product. The project is focused on lithium and boron, which are critical for a sustainable future and are expected to make Ioneer a globally significant, long-life, and low-cost source of these materials. The announcement of the conditional loan commitment was made on January 13, 2023.

Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> Leading U.S. trade associations, the Recycled Materials Association (ReMA) and the International Precious Metals Institute (IPMI), voiced opposition to proposed amendments to the "Preventing Auto Recycling Theft Act" (PART Act) on September 5, 2024. They expressed concern that new traceability measures being considered by the Senate, aimed at curbing catalytic converter theft, could have unintended negative consequences for the industry that recycles critical metals like rhodium, palladium, and platinum. The opposition was formally directed at Senate Amendment 2422 within the proposed National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) for fiscal year 2025, which incorporates the PART Act. The associations argued that while they support the goal of preventing theft, the amendment's current language could disrupt the domestic smelting industry and undermine the supply of these essential precious metals. <2> A Heraeus Precious Metals market report, published on September 10, 2024, outlined the severe financial distress faced by PGM (Platinum Group Metals) miners due to a significant drop in rhodium and palladium prices. The report stated that this price drop has caused revenues to collapse and profit margins to be dramatically reduced. The situation has been worsened by steep mining cost inflation over the last five years, making the highest-cost mining operations unprofitable. North American producers, with a production heavily weighted towards palladium, have also been significantly impacted by cost inflation. At the time of the report, rhodium prices had stabilized around $4,550/oz. <3> A report analyzing the first quarter of 2024 revealed a 9% decrease in new registrations of zero-emission vehicles (ZEVs) in the U.S. compared to the last quarter of 2023, with registrations falling from 385,000 to 352,000. [1] This slowdown was entirely caused by a 12% quarter-on-quarter drop in battery electric vehicle (BEV) registrations, which declined from 302,000 to 265,000. [1] A significant portion of this BEV drop, nearly two-thirds, was attributed to a decline in Tesla Model 3 registrations, while plug-in hybrid electric vehicles (PHEV) continued to show strong growth. [1] As rhodium's primary application, accounting for roughly 90% of its demand, is in catalytic converters for internal combustion engines, a slowdown in the adoption of electric vehicles has a direct impact on rhodium demand. [2, 8] <4> On May 13, 2024, consultancy Metals Focus released a 104-page report forecasting that the average price of rhodium is expected to fall by 28% to $4,750 per troy ounce in 2024. This information was reported by news outlets such as Reuters on the same day. <5> In a report published on May 13, 2024, the consultancy Metals Focus projected that the average price for rhodium is expected to fall by 28% to $4,750 per troy ounce for the 2024 calendar year. This forecast was issued despite the firm's concurrent analysis that the rhodium market would be in a structural deficit for the same period. <6> Throughout 2023, a significant drop in the prices of rhodium and palladium placed immense pressure on the profit margins of Platinum Group Metal (PGM) producers in South Africa. Rhodium prices fell by approximately 63% and palladium by 38-44% during the year. [4, 6, 11] This downturn, which Impala Platinum's CEO noted happened much faster than anticipated, led to sharply lower earnings and dividend cuts for major mining companies. [2, 4] By the end of 2023, an estimated half of all PGM production (excluding Russian output) was considered unprofitable on an all-in sustaining cost basis, according to an analyst from Noah Capital Markets. [6] The World Platinum Investment Council offered a more conservative estimate in December 2023, suggesting 35% of non-Russian PGM output was loss-making at spot prices. [17] In response, mining companies began implementing cost-cutting measures, curbing capital expenditure, and considering workforce reductions to remain viable. [6, 12, 15] <7> A report from the Rhodium Group revealed that US investment in clean energy and transportation surged to a record $67 billion in the fourth quarter of 2023, marking a 40% increase from the same period in 2022. The report, published on February 29, 2024, also highlighted that the fastest investment growth occurred in emerging climate technologies, which saw a tenfold annual increase from $0.9 billion in 2022 to $9.1 billion in 2023. This includes sectors like clean hydrogen, which could potentially drive future demand for rhodium in catalysis. <8> Lifezone Metals Limited has announced the signing of a term sheet with a Glencore plc subsidiary to establish a US-based recycling project for platinum, palladium, and rhodium (PGMs). This joint venture will utilize Lifezone's hydrometallurgical technology to recover these metals from used automotive catalytic converters, aiming for a cleaner and more efficient process than traditional smelting. The project will be implemented in two phases, with the initial phase involving confirmatory piloting and a feasibility study at Lifezone's labs in Perth, Australia. This first phase, expected to be completed in the first half of 2024, is funded with $3 million, contributed equally by both companies. Upon successful completion, the second phase will involve the joint funding and construction of a commercial-scale recycling facility in the United States, with an estimated initial capital cost of $15-20 million. <9> On February 24, 2023, the White House announced new import tariffs on a range of Russian products, which were officially published in the Federal Register on March 2, 2023. While overall imports from Russia have significantly decreased since 2022, the U.S. continues to import strategic commodities, including PGMs like palladium. These tariffs and other sanctions are intended to disrupt Russian revenue. However, analysts note that the global PGM market is resilient, and Russian metals often continue to flow by being rerouted to other sanction-agnostic regions. Russia remains a major global supplier of PGMs, accounting for a significant portion of the world's primary supply.

Prediction target period: from 2026-02-09 to 2026-02-24. The report forecasts that slower-than-expected battery electric vehicle (BEV) adoption in the United States and Europe could support extended gasoline and hybrid vehicle production. Consequently, this sustained production could provide a potential upside for rhodium demand and prices in 2026, with accompanying forecasts indicating rhodium prices could reach between $6,000 and $9,000 per ounce despite the market's inherent volatility. <3> Noble6, a US-based catalytic converter recycling firm, released a market update advising recyclers on inventory strategies amid the largest Platinum Group Metals (PGM) price move in almost 40 years. The update, aimed at increasing industry transparency and profits, highlighted a December 2025 market shock where platinum jumped nearly 40% in a single month. <4> Advanced Remarketing Services published its Q4 2025 Markets & Metals report, noting that U.S. rhodium prices were supported by the lowest above-ground stocks in 40 years, which kept catalytic converter theft a persistent high risk domestically. <5> According to a December 15, 2025, SEC filing, U.S. firm FNY Investment Advisers LLC initiated a new $4.82 million position in Sibanye-Stillwater. This significant transaction propelled the stock into the investment firm's top five holdings, underscoring strong institutional investor interest in major rhodium and platinum group metal (PGM) producers with U.S. operations. <6> Heraeus Precious Metals has released its 2026 Precious Metals Forecast, predicting that the rhodium market could transition from a small deficit to a surplus. The forecast establishes a target price range for rhodium between $6,000 and $9,000 per ounce. Additionally, Heraeus analysts cautioned that an anticipated economic downturn and a potential U.S. recession remain primary downside risks that could negatively impact the prices of platinum group metals (PGMs). <7> On December 4, 2025, Phoenix Refining published a retrospective market report titled 'The Great Rhodium Unwind.' The report provides a detailed analysis of the significant price fluctuations and structural market shifts within the global rhodium sector leading up to the end of 2025. <8> Mining company Sibanye-Stillwater, operator of the U.S.-based Stillwater PGM complex, announced a tripling of its third-quarter earnings, with adjusted EBITDA surging to R9.9 billion (US$560 million). This significant financial turnaround was driven by substantial price improvements in rhodium and other platinum group metals (PGMs), which successfully returned the company's U.S. operations to profitability. <9> On October 14, 2025, it was reported that the average global rhodium price in September 2025 was $279,475.16 per kilogram; The average global rhodium price in September 2025 was a 3.6% increase from the previous month.; This rise was primarily attributed to strong demand from the automotive industry for catalytic converters. <10> A forecast published on September 7, 2025, predicted that rhodium prices could reach $8,000 per troy ounce by the fourth quarter of 2025. The prediction is attributed to ongoing supply constraints and a surge in demand from two key areas: increased production of hybrid vehicles and stricter emission standards in China, specifically the 'China VI-b' policy, which requires more rhodium in catalytic converters. This forecast was issued after rhodium prices had already surged 35% in July 2025 to $7,475 per troy ounce.
